History of Present Illness:
72-year-old woman. Two days of reduced appetite, fatigue and mild right-sided abdominal pain. She denies vomiting or diarrhea.

Physical Examination:
Localized right lower-quadrant tenderness without generalized peritoneal signs. Temperature 37.7 C; heart rate 112/min; BP 122/70 mmHg; respiratory rate 18/min; SpO2 98% on room air.

Laboratory Tests:
WBC: 16.2 10^9/L (reference 4.0-11.0)
Hemoglobin: 13.1 g/dL (reference 12.0-17.5)
Platelets: 283 10^9/L (reference 150-400)
Sodium: 136 mmol/L (reference 135-145)
Potassium: 3.7 mmol/L (reference 3.5-5.0)
Creatinine: 0.9 mg/dL (reference 0.6-1.3)
CRP: 126 mg/L (reference <5)
Lipase: 41 U/L (reference 13-60)
ALT: 31 U/L (reference 7-45)
AST: 26 U/L (reference 10-40)
Alkaline phosphatase: 103 U/L (reference 40-130)
Total bilirubin: 0.7 mg/dL (reference 0.2-1.2)

Imaging Findings:
CT abdomen/pelvis: appendix measures 10 mm with enhancing thickened wall and adjacent stranding; cecum has no focal mass.
